sop_modules.name: Garage Door Protection & Equipment Setup
sop_modules.description: Deploy driveway/apron protection (canvas drops — NOT poly sheeting, safety hazard on hardscapes), mask adjacent siding (spray method), mask window inserts (if present), protect weatherstripping (low-tack tape into channel), mask track/hardware/spring mechanism, manage bottom seal (remove or mask), set up spray equipment with garage-door-specific tips.

tasks.name: Driveway/Apron Protection
tasks.description: Deploy canvas drop cloths or absorbent mats over driveway/apron surface within 6-8 feet of garage door base. Canvas provides non-slip surface and absorbs drips. NEVER use standard poly sheeting on hardscapes — becomes extremely slippery when wet with paint overspray. Secure edges against wind. For spray: extend coverage to full overspray containment zone.

quality_notes.all: Full driveway coverage within overspray zone. Canvas ONLY — no poly on hardscapes. Secure against wind. Extend for spray method.

tasks.name: Adjacent Siding Masking
tasks.description: Apply pre-taped poly or masking film to siding panels flanking the garage door opening. Overspray from garage door spray hits adjacent siding. Tape at edge of garage door casing, extend film 4-6 feet beyond opening on each side. Only required for spray application method.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of adjacent siding. Tape sealed at casing edge. Film extends 4-6 ft beyond opening.

tasks.name: Garage Door Window Insert Masking
tasks.description: Apply HDPE static-cling masking film to window inserts in garage door panels (typically top panel). Edge-seal with UV-resistant tape at glass-to-frame junction. Carriage-style divided-lite windows require individual pane masking — significantly more time. Only applies when garage door has window inserts.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete glass coverage. Tape sealed tight at frame edge.
quality_notes.QT4: Complete coverage. Inspect for bleed-through potential. Crisp masking lines.

tasks.name: Weatherstrip Protection
tasks.description: Push low-tack tape deep into weatherstrip channel along sides and top of garage door using putty knife. Prevents paint from contacting weatherstripping material. Paint on weatherstripping destroys seal flexibility — causes brittleness and seal failure. Approximately 35-40 LF of weatherstrip per standard garage door.

quality_notes.all: Tape fully seated in channel with putty knife. No gaps. Complete perimeter coverage (sides + top).

tasks.name: Track & Hardware Masking
tasks.description: Mask all track and roller contact points, spring mechanism hardware, cables, and brackets with tape and plastic film. These components must NOT be painted — paint causes binding, stalling, and potential spring/motor damage. Cover hardware areas visible from spray zone. Mask from garage interior side.

quality_notes.all: ALL moving parts masked — tracks, rollers, springs, cables, brackets. No paint on any mechanical component.

tasks.name: Bottom Seal Management
tasks.description: Prepare bottom weatherseal (astragal) for painting cycle. Preferred: remove seal and retainer entirely for clean access to bottom panel edge and six-side seal on wood doors. Alternative: mask seal in place with tape, plan to prop door 2-4 inches during cure. Bottom seal bonds to wet paint — management is MANDATORY.

quality_notes.all: Either remove seal completely (preferred) or mask thoroughly. Document removal for reinstall. Plan for prop-open cure.

tasks.name: Spray Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Configure airless sprayer with garage-door-specific tips: 310 tip (0.010 inch orifice, 6-inch fan) for steel doors, 412 tip (0.012 inch, 8-inch fan) for double-door faces. Install 100-mesh blue filter for enamel on steel. Stage 2.5-inch angled sash brush for panel recess detail work on raised-panel and carriage doors.

quality_notes.all: Verify tip size matches substrate and door size. Test spray pattern on cardboard. Stage brush for panel detail work.

tasks.name: Brush Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Stage brushes for brush-only application: 2.5-inch angled sash brush for faces and panel recesses, 2-inch flat brush for edge work. Paint pots and materials. Brush method is secondary — typically used only for panel recess detail on raised-panel and carriage doors, or when spray is not feasible.

quality_notes.all: Stage materials within reach. Brush method only when spray is not feasible.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Driveway protection first -> Adjacent siding masking (spray) -> Window masking (if present) -> Weatherstrip protection -> Track/hardware masking -> Bottom seal management -> Equipment setup last.

sop_modules.name: Garage Door Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: Substrate-driven preparation. Steel: factory wax removal (3M gray synthetic steel wool pad + biodegradable cleaner) -> degloss sand (120-150 grit) -> ASTM D3359 adhesion test. Wood: sand -> fill defects -> tannin spot prime (cedar/redwood). Carriage: mixed-material prep per overlay type. Wax removal on steel is CRITICAL — #1 failure mode is painting over residual factory wax.

tasks.name: Factory Wax Removal (Steel)
tasks.description: Scuff entire steel door face with gray 3M synthetic steel wool pad (#000 equivalent) saturated with biodegradable cleaning solution. Removes residual factory wax, silicone release agents, and surface contaminants from fabrication and transit. Use SYNTHETIC steel wool only — real steel wool leaves ferrous residue that causes rust staining. Wax removal is MANDATORY before any other prep step. Without it, new acrylic over factory finish results in catastrophic peeling.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Factory-primed steel has wax contamination from fabrication. Wax removal is MANDATORY.
Bare metal (factory primer damaged) still needs surface decontamination.

quality_notes.all: Complete surface coverage. Verify with clean white rag — no residue transfer = clean. Gray pads only, never real steel wool. 2 pads per single door, 3 per double.

tasks.name: Degloss Sand Factory Finish (Steel)
tasks.description: Sand steel door face with 120-150 grit to degloss factory fluorocarbon/polyester finish and create mechanical tooth for primer adhesion. Performed AFTER wax removal. Even scratch pattern across entire door face. Chemical deglosser (liquid) is acceptable alternative to mechanical sanding.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Factory finish requires degloss for mechanical adhesion.
Bare metal: sand to remove light oxidation and create profile.

quality_notes.QT3: Even scuff pattern. No glossy patches remaining.
quality_notes.QT4: Full surface sand with systematic coverage. Feather all scratches. Raking light inspect.

tasks.name: ASTM D3359 Adhesion Test (Steel)
tasks.description: Perform ASTM D3359 cross-hatch tape adhesion test on deglossed factory finish to verify mechanical bond. Apply test tape over cross-hatch cuts, pull at 180 degrees, evaluate adhesion rating. If adhesion test FAILS (rating < 4B), escalate to more aggressive removal or Brush-Off Blast Cleaning (SSPC-SP7). Quality checkpoint before primer application.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Adhesion test verifies wax removal and degloss were effective on factory finish.
Adhesion test verifies clean bare metal profile.

quality_notes.all: Test in 2-3 locations per door (top, middle, bottom panel). Minimum 4B rating required. Document results. If fail: re-prep or escalate to SSPC-SP7.

tasks.name: Sand Wood Garage Door
tasks.description: Sand all wood garage door surfaces with 120-150 grit. Remove mill glaze, open wood grain for primer adhesion. Hand sand panel recesses and profiles. Orbital sander for flat panel faces. Include all panel edges accessible through articulation joints.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Bare wood requires full sanding to remove mill glaze and open grain.

quality_notes.QT3: Full surface sand. Even scratch pattern. No glossy patches.
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic sand with full coverage. Inspect all edges and recesses. Raking light verify.

tasks.name: Fill Wood Door Defects
tasks.description: Fill nail holes, minor defects, and small damage on wood garage door panels with exterior-rated wood filler. Allow to cure per manufacturer spec. Sand flush with 150-220 grit. Most NC wood garage doors have minimal defects.

substrate_state_rules.notes: New wood may have minor defects, machining marks.

quality_notes.QT4: Fill all defects > 1/16 inch. Sand flush. Verify with raking light.

tasks.name: Tannin Knot Spot Prime (Wood)
tasks.description: Spot-apply alkyd stain-blocking primer (SYS_EXT_GRDR_PRIMER_ALKYD_STAINBLOCK) to visible knots on tannin-rich wood species (cedar, redwood, Douglas fir). Brush apply to individual knots BEFORE full acrylic primer coat. For severe tannin species, may apply full-surface instead of spot. Prevents brown/yellow stain bleed-through on finish coat.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Tannin-rich bare wood species need spot prime on knots before full acrylic primer.

quality_notes.QT3: Spot prime visible knots. Complete seal over each knot.
quality_notes.QT4: Spot prime all knots including small ones. Extended coverage around knot area.

tasks.name: Carriage-Style Mixed-Material Prep
tasks.description: Prep carriage-style door with mixed materials. Steel base: wax removal + degloss per steel protocol. Wood overlays: sand per wood protocol. Composite overlays: light scuff sand if matte, or assess for bonding primer need if glossy/sealed. Each material type on the same door may require different prep approach. Mask decorative hardware and overlay edges to prevent cross-contamination.

quality_notes.QT3: Each material prepped per its protocol. No cross-contamination.
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic mixed-material prep. Document overlay surface condition for primer selection.

tasks.name: Dust Removal After Prep
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust from garage door surfaces, panel recesses, articulation joints, and edges using tack cloth. Ensure zero dust contamination before primer application. Critical to clean articulation joint areas where dust collects.

quality_notes.all: Complete dust removal including articulation joints and panel recesses. White rag verification on steel surfaces.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Steel: wax removal -> degloss sand -> adhesion test -> dust removal. Wood: sand -> fill defects -> tannin spot prime -> dust removal. Carriage: mixed-material prep -> dust removal.

sop_modules.name: Garage Door Primer Application
sop_modules.description: Substrate-driven primer: DTM primer for steel (SYS_EXT_GRDR_PRIMER_DTM — mandatory even over factory primer due to wax contamination), 100% acrylic primer for wood (SYS_EXT_GRDR_PRIMER_ACRYLIC), bonding primer for carriage composite overlays (SYS_EXT_GRDR_PRIMER_BONDING — conditional on glossy surface). LEAPFROG TECHNIQUE MANDATORY: paint alternating panels (1,3,5 then 2,4,6), opening each joint to dry tack-free before painting adjacent. Never prime in fully closed position. Wood doors: six-side seal primer per DASMA TDS #162. CRITICAL: bare ferrous metal must be primed same day as surface prep.

tasks.name: Spray DTM Primer — Steel Garage Door
tasks.description: Apply acrylic DTM (Direct-to-Metal) primer to steel garage door face using airless sprayer. Rust-inhibitive pigments provide sacrificial barrier protection. LEAPFROG TECHNIQUE: prime alternating panels (1,3,5), open joints to dry tack-free, then prime remaining panels (2,4,6). Even wet coat per manufacturer mil spec. 310 tip for single door, 412 tip for double door. CRITICAL: bare ferrous metal must be primed same day as prep — oxidation begins within hours.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Factory-primed steel STILL gets DTM primer — factory finish is unreliable after wax removal. DTM provides fresh adhesion bridge.
Bare steel requires DTM primer. Must prime same day as prep.

quality_notes.all: LEAPFROG: alternate panels, open joints, tack-free between. Even wet coat. No holidays. Target 1.5 mils DFT.

tasks.name: Brush DTM Primer — Steel Garage Door
tasks.description: Apply DTM primer to steel garage door face by brush when spray is not feasible. Same DTM chemistry as spray. LEAPFROG TECHNIQUE still applies: brush alternating panels, open joints, tack-free between. Brush provides better control on panel recesses and edge detail.

substrate_state_rules.notes: Factory-primed steel STILL gets DTM primer.

quality_notes.all: LEAPFROG technique. Even coat, no drips. Complete coverage. Same-day prime on bare metal.

tasks.name: Spray Acrylic Primer — Wood Garage Door
tasks.description: Apply 100% acrylic latex exterior primer (SYS_EXT_GRDR_PRIMER_ACRYLIC) to wood garage door face using airless sprayer. LEAPFROG TECHNIQUE: prime alternating panels, open joints, tack-free between. Six-side sealing per DASMA TDS #162 — primer must cover exterior face, all panel edges accessible through articulation joints. Back face and hidden edges require separate access (see TSK_GRDR_PRIME_SIX_SIDE).

substrate_state_rules.notes: Bare wood requires full primer coat.

quality_notes.all: LEAPFROG technique. Even wet coat. No holidays. 100% acrylic primer. Six-side sealing obligation.

tasks.name: Brush Acrylic Primer — Wood Garage Door
tasks.description: Apply 100% acrylic exterior primer to wood garage door face by brush. LEAPFROG TECHNIQUE applies. Six-side sealing per DASMA TDS #162. Brush provides better penetration into wood grain and panel recesses.

quality_notes.all: LEAPFROG technique. Even coat, no drips. Complete coverage including edges at articulation joints.

tasks.name: Bonding Primer — Carriage Composite Overlays
tasks.description: Apply bonding primer (SYS_EXT_GRDR_PRIMER_BONDING) to glossy/sealed composite overlay panels on carriage-style doors. Grips slick composite while providing tooth for topcoat. Steel base of carriage door gets DTM primer separately. Conditional — only needed when composite overlays reject standard primers (glossy/sealed surface). Must be topcoated within 1 week.

quality_notes.all: Apply to overlay surfaces only. Steel base gets DTM separately. Must topcoat within 1 week — bonding primer becomes brittle if left exposed.

tasks.name: Six-Side Seal Primer — Wood Door Edges and Back Face
tasks.description: Brush primer on all hidden surfaces of wood garage door per DASMA TDS #162: back face (garage-interior side), top edge, bottom edge, and side edges. End-grain (top/bottom) absorbs more primer — apply heavier at edges. Back face access may require painting panels individually before assembly or with door propped open for access. Failure to seal all six sides causes moisture wicking, rot, panel distortion, and warranty voidance.

substrate_state_rules.notes: All bare wood doors require six-side sealing per DASMA TDS #162.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete coverage all 6 sides. Heavy application at end-grain edges.
quality_notes.QT4: Complete six-side coverage. Inspect with flashlight/mirror. Confirm no holidays at edges and back face.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Steel: DTM primer (spray or brush, leapfrog) -> complete. Wood: tannin spot prime (done in prep) -> acrylic primer face (leapfrog) -> six-side seal edges/back face. Carriage: DTM on steel base + bonding on composite overlays -> complete. CRITICAL: bare metal primed same day as prep.

sop_modules.name: Garage Door First Finish Coat
sop_modules.description: First finish coat application. Spray is primary method for garage door faces — large flat panels ideal for airless spray. LEAPFROG TECHNIQUE MANDATORY: spray alternating panels (1,3,5 then 2,4,6), opening each joint to dry tack-free before painting adjacent. Prevents articulation joint paint bridging (critical failure mode). Brush detail for panel recesses on raised-panel and carriage-style doors. Roller is NOT valid for metal doors (introduces orange peel). Standard acrylic (QT3, SYS_EXT_GRDR_FINISH_STANDARD) or premium acrylic (QT4, SYS_EXT_GRDR_FINISH_PREMIUM).

tasks.name: Spray First Finish Coat — Garage Door Face
tasks.description: Spray first finish coat on garage door exterior face using airless sprayer. LEAPFROG TECHNIQUE: spray alternating panels (1,3,5), open each joint, verify tack-free, then spray remaining panels (2,4,6). 310 tip for single door, 412 for double. Maintain even wet coat with consistent mil build. Do NOT back-roll on metal — orange peel is undesirable. 100% acrylic exterior latex per quality tier.

quality_notes.QT3: LEAPFROG. Even coat, no runs or sags. Clean edges. Verify no joint bridging.
quality_notes.QT4: LEAPFROG. Even coat with premium material. Inspect for holidays, runs, sags. Verify no joint bridging. Raking light before dry.

tasks.name: Brush First Finish Coat — Garage Door Face
tasks.description: Brush first finish coat on garage door face when spray is not feasible. LEAPFROG TECHNIQUE: brush alternating panels, open joints, tack-free between. Long even strokes. Maintain wet edge. Brush method is significantly slower than spray on garage door faces — use only when spray is not available.

quality_notes.QT3: LEAPFROG. Even coat, no lap marks. Clean edges.
quality_notes.QT4: LEAPFROG. Even coat with premium material. Tip off brush marks while wet.

tasks.name: Brush Panel Recesses — First Finish Coat
tasks.description: Brush finish coat into panel recesses on raised-panel and carriage-style garage doors. Work recesses BEFORE face spray to allow wet-on-wet blend at recess-to-face transition. Angled sash brush for recess detail. Carriage overlay detail work — crossbuck grooves, decorative hardware surrounds.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete recess coverage. No puddles in corners. Clean transition to face.
quality_notes.QT4: Complete coverage. Thin even coat. No buildup at panel-to-face transition.

tasks.name: Leapfrog Joint Separation Verification — Coat 1
tasks.description: After first coat application, verify all articulation joints are free and not bridged with paint. Manually articulate each panel joint to confirm separation. If any joint is bridged, immediately break bond while paint is still wet. This is a quality gate — NOT optional. Joint bridging causes catastrophic paint tearing and opener motor damage.

quality_notes.all: MANDATORY check. Articulate every joint. No bridging permitted. Break any wet bridges immediately.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Panel recesses (brush, if raised_panel/carriage) first -> Face spray/brush (leapfrog technique) -> Leapfrog joint separation verification.

sop_modules.name: Garage Door Intercoat Inspection & Sand
sop_modules.description: Between-coat inspection and maintenance. QT3: visual inspect for runs/sags/holidays, touch up defects, re-verify leapfrog joint separation. QT4: light sand 220-grit between finish coats, raking light inspection, dust removal, re-verify joint separation. Runs between finish coat 1 and finish coat 2.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs AFTER first finish coat, BEFORE second finish coat. 1 interstage pass for 2-finish-coat system.

tasks.name: Intercoat Inspection
tasks.description: Inspect first finish coat for runs, sags, drips, holidays, dust nibs, and coverage uniformity across all panels. Check for paint bridging at articulation joints. Mark defects for repair. QT3: visual scan. QT4: raking light inspection.

quality_notes.QT3: Visual scan for obvious defects — runs, sags, holidays. Verify joint separation.
quality_notes.QT4: Raking light inspection. Mark all defects. Check panel recesses for buildup. Verify joint separation.

tasks.name: Intercoat Sand (QT4 Only)
tasks.description: Light scuff sand between finish coats with 220-grit to promote intercoat adhesion and remove minor defects. QT4 only — QT3 gets visual inspect without sanding. Hand sand panel recesses. Orbital for flat faces.

quality_notes.QT4: Light scuff sand. Even scratch pattern. Include panel recesses. No aggressive sanding — just break gloss.

tasks.name: Intercoat Defect Repair
tasks.description: Repair defects found during intercoat inspection: sand out runs/sags, spot-coat holidays, feather drip marks. Address any paint buildup in panel recesses or at articulation joint edges.

quality_notes.QT3: Sand out obvious runs/sags. Spot-coat holidays.
quality_notes.QT4: Full defect repair. Feather all repairs. Re-inspect before coat 2.

tasks.name: Intercoat Dust Removal
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust after intercoat sanding. Tack cloth all surfaces including panel recesses and articulation joint edges. Ensure zero contamination before second finish coat. QT4 only — accompanies intercoat sanding.

quality_notes.all: Complete dust removal. Tack cloth all surfaces including articulation joints.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Allow recoat dry time per product spec -> Inspect (all tiers) -> Sand (QT4 only) -> Repair defects (if found) -> Dust removal (QT4 only) -> Ready for coat 2.

sop_modules.name: Garage Door Second Finish Coat
sop_modules.description: Second finish coat — same leapfrog technique and application method as first coat. All garage doors get 2 finish coats regardless of quality tier. Same material system as coat 1. After coat 2, prop door 2-4 inches above threshold for 24-48 hour cure to prevent bottom seal adhesion.

tasks.name: Spray Second Finish Coat — Garage Door Face
tasks.description: Spray second finish coat. Same LEAPFROG TECHNIQUE as coat 1: alternating panels, open joints, tack-free between. Same tip and material. Final coat — extra care on even coverage and complete film build.

quality_notes.QT3: LEAPFROG. Even coat. Final visual check. Verify no joint bridging.
quality_notes.QT4: LEAPFROG. Even coat with premium material. Raking light before dry. Zero defects.

tasks.name: Brush Second Finish Coat — Garage Door Face
tasks.description: Brush second finish coat. Same LEAPFROG TECHNIQUE as coat 1. Maintain wet edge, long even strokes.

quality_notes.QT3: LEAPFROG. Even coat, no lap marks.
quality_notes.QT4: LEAPFROG. Even coat. Tip off brush marks while wet.

tasks.name: Brush Panel Recesses — Second Finish Coat
tasks.description: Brush second finish coat into panel recesses on raised-panel and carriage-style doors. Same technique as coat 1: recesses before face spray for wet-on-wet blend.

quality_notes.QT4: Thin even coat. No buildup at transitions. Uniform film.

tasks.name: Leapfrog Joint Separation Verification — Coat 2
tasks.description: After second coat, verify all articulation joints are free and not bridged. Same mandatory quality gate as coat 1. Articulate every panel joint to confirm separation.

quality_notes.all: MANDATORY. Articulate every joint. No bridging. Break any wet bridges immediately.

tasks.name: Prop Door Open for Bottom Seal Cure
tasks.description: After final coat, prop garage door 2-4 inches above driveway threshold to prevent bottom weatherseal (astragal) from bonding to wet paint during 24-48 hour cure. Use shims, blocks, or opener chain adjustment. If bottom seal was removed, skip prop and plan reinstall after cure. This task prevents a common callback — seal stuck to driveway tears paint and seal.

quality_notes.all: Door propped 2-4 inches above threshold. Stable prop — will not slip during 24-48 hour cure. Inform homeowner of prop requirement and timeline.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Panel recesses (brush, if raised_panel/carriage) -> Face spray/brush (leapfrog) -> Leapfrog joint verification -> Prop door for bottom seal cure.

sop_modules.name: Garage Door Final Inspection
sop_modules.description: Final walkthrough inspection of completed garage door: verify complete coverage across all panels, no bridged articulation joints, clean masking lines at windows and hardware zones, bottom seal clearance, balance test checkpoint (SOP quality gate — not billable). Touch up any defects found.

tasks.name: Final Door Inspection
tasks.description: Final visual inspection of completed garage door: all panels, articulation joints, panel recesses, window masking lines (if applicable), hardware zone masking lines. Verify complete coverage, uniform sheen, no runs/sags/holidays. Check bottom seal clearance (2-4 inch prop). Mark any touch-up areas.

quality_notes.QT3: Visual scan all panels. Verify joint separation. Check bottom seal prop. Mark touch-ups.
quality_notes.QT4: Raking light inspection all panels. Uniform sheen verification. Joint separation. Window masking lines. Bottom seal clearance.

tasks.name: Balance Test Checkpoint
tasks.description: SOP quality gate (not billable line item): verify garage door balance after painting. A properly balanced door lifts with less than 10 lbs of force. Heavy coatings add weight that can affect counterbalance springs. Disconnect opener, manually lift door halfway, release — should stay in place. If unbalanced, flag for spring adjustment (not painting scope).

quality_notes.all: Disconnect opener. Manual lift test. Door stays at halfway point. If unbalanced, document and flag for customer — spring adjustment is not painting scope.

tasks.name: Touch-Up Minor Defects
tasks.description: Touch up minor defects found during final inspection: small holidays, drips at panel edges, masking bleed-through at windows. Brush touch-up with matching finish. Feather into surrounding area.

quality_notes.QT3: Address obvious defects. Feather into surrounding.
quality_notes.QT4: Address all marked defects. Invisible feather. Re-inspect after touch-up.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Final inspection -> Balance test checkpoint -> Touch-up defects.

sop_modules.name: Garage Door Protection Teardown & Cleanup
sop_modules.description: Remove all protection materials: driveway canvas runners, siding masking, window masking, weatherstrip tape, track/hardware masking. Reinstall bottom seal (if removed). Lower door to threshold (after 24-48 hour cure). Verify door articulates freely (opens/closes without binding). Tool and equipment cleaning.

tasks.name: Window Masking Removal
tasks.description: Remove HDPE static-cling film and edge tape from garage door window inserts. Remove tape at angle to prevent paint film lifting. Clean any adhesive residue from glass. Inspect paint line quality at glass-to-frame edge.

quality_notes.QT3: Remove masking. Clean glass. Verify paint line.
quality_notes.QT4: Remove at angle. Clean residue. Sharp paint line at frame edge.

tasks.name: Weatherstrip Tape Removal
tasks.description: Remove protective tape from weatherstrip channels along sides and top of door. Verify no paint contamination on weatherstripping material. If paint found on weatherstrip, clean immediately — dried paint on weatherstrip causes seal failure.

quality_notes.all: Complete tape removal. Verify no paint on weatherstripping. Clean any contamination immediately.

tasks.name: Track & Hardware Masking Removal
tasks.description: Remove tape and plastic from track, roller, spring, and cable hardware. Verify no paint on any moving parts or contact surfaces. Paint on track or rollers causes binding — clean any contamination immediately.

quality_notes.all: Complete masking removal. ZERO paint on moving parts. Verify track and rollers are clean.

tasks.name: Adjacent Siding Masking Removal
tasks.description: Remove masking film and tape from siding panels adjacent to garage door opening. Fold paint-side-in. Verify no paint drips or overspray on siding surface.

quality_notes.all: Remove masking. Fold paint-side-in. Verify no overspray on siding.

tasks.name: Bottom Seal Reinstallation
tasks.description: Reinstall bottom weatherseal (astragal) and retainer if removed during setup. Only after 24-48 hour cure is complete. Verify seal compression against driveway threshold is correct — should deflect slightly when door closes. If bottom seal was masked in place, remove prop blocks and lower door after cure.

quality_notes.all: Seal correctly seated. Proper compression against threshold. No paint bonding seal to driveway.

tasks.name: Driveway Protection Teardown
tasks.description: Remove canvas drop cloths and absorbent mats from driveway/apron. Fold paint-side-in. Verify no paint drips on driveway surface. Clean any drips immediately — dried paint on broom-finish concrete is nearly impossible to remove.

quality_notes.all: Fold paint-side-in. Clean driveway surface. No paint residue on hardscape.

tasks.name: Door Articulation Test
tasks.description: Verify garage door opens and closes freely without binding, paint tearing, or mechanical resistance. Reconnect opener. Test full cycle: open, stop at midpoint, close. Listen for unusual sounds. Verify no paint bridging at any articulation joint. This is the final quality gate — door must operate normally.

quality_notes.all: Full open/close cycle. No binding. No paint tearing at joints. Opener functions normally. No unusual sounds.

tasks.name: Tool and Equipment Cleaning
tasks.description: Clean all brushes, spray equipment (flush lines, clean tip and filter), and tools. Proper cleaning of angled sash brushes for reuse. Flush airless sprayer with water (latex materials). Dispose of used synthetic steel wool pads properly.

quality_notes.all: Full equipment clean. Brushes shaped and stored. Spray lines flushed. Steel wool pads disposed.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Window unmask -> Weatherstrip unmask -> Track/hardware unmask -> Siding unmask (if spray) -> Bottom seal reinstall (after 24-48 hr cure) -> Driveway teardown -> Articulation test -> Tool cleaning.

round_configurations.description: 1 primer coat + 2 finish coats — standard NC for ALL garage door substrates. Factory-primed steel STILL gets DTM primer (wax contamination). No skip-prime path.

applicability_rules.description: Steel-specific tasks activate only for steel substrate
Wood-specific tasks activate only for wood substrate
Carriage-specific tasks activate only for carriage substrate
Window masking tasks activate only when door has windows
Panel recess brush tasks activate for raised_panel and carriage complexity
Spray equipment and spray application tasks activate only for spray method
Brush-only equipment and face tasks activate only for brush method
Intercoat sanding and dust removal are QT4 only — QT3 gets visual inspect only

exclusions.description: Garage door casing/trim painting — belongs to SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1
exclusions.scope: Casing and trim surround prep, prime, and paint are NOT in this spec. This spec covers the garage door panel assembly (exterior face) only.

exclusions.description: Garage interior (garage-side) face — not exterior spec scope
exclusions.scope: Interior face of the garage door is not scoped under this exterior painting spec. DASMA TDS #162 six-side sealing for wood doors includes back face primer but not full decorative finish.

exclusions.description: Roller application on metal doors — introduces orange peel
exclusions.scope: Roller is NOT a valid application method for steel or carriage-style garage doors. Spray is primary; brush is for detail work on panel recesses and edges only.

exclusions.description: QT2 and QT5 excluded for garage doors
exclusions.scope: QT2 excluded — garage doors are visible from street, not economy-appropriate. QT5 excluded — utility surface, not architectural showcase. Valid tiers: QT3-QT4.

exclusions.description: Spring and opener mechanism repair — not painting scope
exclusions.scope: Spring balance adjustment, opener motor repair, and track alignment are NOT painting scope. Balance test checkpoint is a quality gate only — if unbalanced, flag for separate trade.
Entry door painting uses separate spec, separate PS key (PS_EXT_OPENING_EA.DOOR_EXT vs PS_EXT_OPENING_EA.DOOR_GARAGE), and separate context prefix (XDOR vs GRDR).

assumptions.value: Factory-primed steel garage doors STILL require DTM primer — no skip-prime path unlike entry doors
assumptions.note: Wax contamination from fabrication makes factory primer unreliable. DTM primer provides fresh adhesion bridge after wax removal.

assumptions.value: All garage door substrates use same round config: 1 prime + 2 finish coats. No skip-prime path.
assumptions.note: Simplifies to one round config vs entry doors which have two (bare substrate vs factory-primed).

assumptions.value: Back face of wood garage doors receives primer + 1 finish coat (sealing obligation) — not full 2-coat decorative finish
assumptions.note: DASMA requires all six sides sealed. Minimum compliance: primer + 1 coat on back face. Full 2-coat back face would be a scope add-on.

assumptions.value: Leapfrog technique modifies HOW prime/finish tasks are executed — it is a process note, not a separate billable task. Leapfrog joint verification IS a separate inspection task.
assumptions.note: Leapfrog is embedded in each spray/brush task description. Joint verification is an explicit checkpoint task.

assumptions.value: Door must be propped open 2-4 inches above threshold during 24-48 hour cure
assumptions.note: Standard practice. Bottom seal bonds to wet paint on driveway threshold — tearing seal and paint on reopening.

garage_specific_features: LEAPFROG TECHNIQUE — embedded in all prime/finish task descriptions, explicit joint verification tasks after each coat
BOTTOM SEAL MANAGEMENT — dedicated setup/maintain/reinstall tasks across 3 modules
FACTORY WAX REMOVAL — steel-specific prep task unique to garage doors (not shared with entry doors)
ASTM D3359 ADHESION TEST — mandatory quality gate on steel after degloss
SIX-SIDE SEAL — wood-specific primer task for DASMA TDS #162 compliance
BALANCE TEST CHECKPOINT — quality gate (not billable) for spring tension verification
DRIVEWAY SAFETY — canvas ONLY protection (no poly on hardscapes)
NO ROLLER ON METAL — enforced through exclusion rules
